title: EPB and IonQ Deploy Hybrid Trapped-Ion Algorithms on Forte Enterprise to Optimize Power Grid Topology - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Chattanooga utility EPB and IonQ published three preprints, funded by a $4M NIST grant, running hybrid quantum-classical distribution network reconfiguration algorithms on an on-premises IonQ Forte Enterprise at networks up to 417 buses. Results include a 95.8% parameter cut for quantum-enhanced RL and a 40x faster Gurobi MISOCP solve with quantum hints, but end-to-end runtime only starts to narrow versus classical at the largest 417-bus system.

insights.claim: Enforcing radiality through penalty terms in QUBO matrices introduces artificial energy barriers and barren plateaus, which is why the teams used topology-preserving encodings instead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Naive QUBO formulations are a structural weakness of quantum optimization; constraint-native encodings are the better design.

insights.claim: A quantum-enhanced Double DQN with a 4-layer parameterized quantum circuit backbone cut parameters by 95.8% on the IEEE 33-bus system (9,156 vs 220,052 classically).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum circuits may serve as parameter-efficient function approximators in RL.

insights.claim: Running the Q-DRL model on IonQ Forte Enterprise hardware found the exact optimum (0.1396 MW loss) for the 33-bus system and came within 0.30% of optimum for the 69-bus system.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware noise did not prevent optimal solutions at small grid sizes.

insights.claim: Subspace LR-QAOA hints, using a fixed 29-qubit budget, cut median Gurobi MISOCP solver runtime to reach within 1% of target from 1,415.47 s to 34.71 s on a 417-bus network.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum as a warm-start/hint generator for classical solvers is the most credible near-term optimization pattern.

insights.claim: Warm-start iterative QITE recovered global minimal-loss configurations on six benchmark networks and converged within 0.2% to 2.18% of reference losses on larger systems up to 415 buses.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multiple algorithm families produced near-optimal answers, reducing single-method risk.

insights.claim: In the two-stage MISOCP workflow, end-to-end runtime on small and medium networks was dominated by quantum circuit overhead and classical pre- and post-processing, eroding the solver-time gains.

insights.so_what: Solver-only speedups overstate practical value; total pipeline time is what utilities pay for.
